newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.01 pct in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.01 pct in quiet session.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped a slight 0.01 percent to close at 1.0628 per dollar in sluggish trading on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $169 million surplus on Tuesday.
Dealers expect the Central Bank to lower the mini-band on Wednesday by 0.05 percent to between 1.0630 and 1.0680 reais per dollar.
"Tomorrow is the last day of the month and the Central Bank always changes the mini-band on this day," a trader said.
The Central Bank last lowered the mini-band on April 22 to between 1.0625 and 1.0675 reais per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.52 percent against the dollar compared to an average drop of between 0.5 and 0.6 percent over the past three months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real ended steady at 1.0676 per greenback.
In the parallel market, the real also closed flat at 1.132 per dollar, traders added.
